subject: SLA template — uptime threshold and blended monthly credit model
messages:
From: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@atlasdata.com>
To: grace_oconnor@redwood.com, laura_bennett@redwood.com
Cc: contracts@atlasdata.com
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2025 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SLA template: uptime % and monthly credits — Atlas draft attached

Hi Grace / Laura,

Thanks again for the demo last week — Atlas is excited about the latency profile you showed. Our procurement team has drafted an SLA to include with the SOW. Two things we're looking to clarify before legal signs off:

1) Uptime baseline: our legal team expects a 99.95% floor for hosted inference endpoints.
2) Monthly service credit model: we'd like a straightforward remedy that scales with minutes of unavailability rather than an absolute cap.

Attached is our starting point (atlas_draft_sla_v3.pdf). Can you confirm whether Redwood can accept 99.95 as the standard or propose an alternative that preserves the same economic protection? Also, we'd like to include a latency clause for p95 > 200ms to trigger partial credits.

Short answers would be great — our cycle is tight.

Thanks,
Sophie
Sophie Martin
Procurement Lead, Atlas Data
attachments: [atlas_draft_sla_v3.pdf (pdf)]

From: grace_oconnor@redwood.com
To: Sophie Martin <sophie.martin@atlasdata.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.com, contracts@atlasdata.com
Date: Sun, 21 Sep 2025 12:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: SLA template: uptime % and monthly credits — Atlas draft attached

Hi Sophie — thanks for sending the draft and for the fast turnaround. We're aligned on the goal of keeping Atlas protected while preserving operational flexibility. A few proposals from our side: 

• Baseline uptime: propose a standard 99.95% for hosted endpoints, with explicit regional carve-outs for scheduled maintenance windows (72 hours notice for >30m planned events).
• Blended monthly credit model: rather than a single-step cap, we propose a bucketed credit schedule:
  - 99.95%–99.90% => 5% of that month's invoice as credit
  - 99.90%–99.80% => 10% credit
  - <99.80% => 20% credit (capped at a maximum of 20% monthly invoice)
• Latency: propose a partial remedy for sustained p95 latency breaches (>200ms for more than 12 hours in a rolling 30-day window) that yields a 2% credit per incident, stacking up to 6% per month.
• Calculation examples: we'll include a worked example to show how credits would be computed for typical months.

I've attached a concise proposal PDF (redwood_blended_sla_proposal.pdf) that mirrors your structure but incorporates the sliding credit bands and a latency carve-in. If Atlas prefers a fixed cap instead of a percentage-of-invoice approach, we can provide an alternate table.

Proposed next step: quick call tomorrow to walk the algebra on the credits — 20 minutes should do it. What time works for you?

Best,
Grace O'Connor
Head of Revenue Operations
Redwood Inference

Grace — thanks for the fast reply and the draft schedule. A couple of clarifying items from Atlas legal/procurement: 

1) The bucketed percentage model looks promising, but legal wants one worked example for how credits are computed in a 720-hour billing month. For example: if we have 45 minutes of unplanned downtime to a single regional endpoint (hosted, not private) how does that map to 99.95 vs. 99.90 and what credit applies?
2) For latency, can you clarify what constitutes an "incident" for the p95 trigger (is it a single-hour window, sustained multi-hour window, and how is aggregation handled across regions)?
3) Finally, legal wants to cap monthly credits to a portion of the monthly invoice (they suggested 15%); Redwood's earlier note of 20% is probably acceptable if we can agree on a temporary pilot cap at 10% for the first 3 months post-launch.

If you can send the worked calculation and a sentence defining the latency incident aggregation, we can get this to our legal team by EOD tomorrow.

Appreciate it — Sophie

Sophie — thanks for the specific asks. Below are concrete answers and a worked example you can share with legal.

1) Worked example (720-hour month):
   - 720 hours = 43,200 minutes.
   - 45 minutes of unplanned downtime -> availability = (43,200 - 45) / 43,200 = 0.9989583 = 99.89583%
   - That maps to the 99.90%–99.80% bucket (since availability rounded to two decimals is 99.90% threshold crossed), so Atlas would receive a 10% credit on that month's Redwood-hosted invoice per the proposed bucket table.

2) Latency incident definition and aggregation:
   - Incident: any contiguous window where p95 latency for the affected endpoint exceeds 200ms for at least 60 minutes.
   - Aggregation: incidents separated by less than 120 minutes are merged; separate regions are assessed independently and credits are additive but subject to the monthly cap.

3) Monthly cap and pilot:
   - We can accept a capped approach. Standard cap = 20% of the monthly invoice (as a protective ceiling). However, Redwood is willing to run a 3-month launch pilot with Atlas where the cap is 10% to limit early-stage exposure. After the pilot, the cap reverts to the contracted cap (e.g., 20%) unless both parties agree to change it.

4) Maintenance carve-outs and notice:
   - Planned maintenance (any window >30 minutes) is a carve-out when Redwood provides >=72 hours notice and a mitigation plan. Emergency maintenance for critical security fixes is carve-out with post-event notification.

Next steps: If that lines up with Atlas legal, we'll update the draft SLA and send a DocuSign to the primary contract contact. To keep timelines tight, would you sign the 3-month pilot clause and the worked example? I'll include the DocuSign link and short markup in my next send.

Best regards,
Laura Bennett
Director, Commercial Contracts
Redwood Inference
